The park alternative will have none of the proposed plan's non-park related undesirable environmental impacts. Avoidance of most of the proposed plan's adverse impacts would be a favorable element of the park alternative. Conversely, since this alternative does not contain the housing, neighborhood revitalization, public works and social programs of the proposed plan, it cannot have the beneficial effects associated with these programs. Its failure to have these beneficial effects must be considered a negative aspect of this alternative in comparison with the proposed plan. As with the rehabilitation alternative, this alternative concentrates on only one element of neighborhood improvement to the exclusion of the other more varied programs contained in the proposed plan.
Street Improvement Alternative
The street improvement alternative consists of residential street improvements as contained in the proposed plan for the Northside, Gardner, and Alviso rehabilitation areas, and those proposed for other areas. Remaining block grant funds would be applied to other similar street projects within San Jose. Major components of this alternative include repaving, the installation of curbs, sidewalks, local drainage facilities, street lighting and landscaping, standardization of street widths, and the inter-connection of the stub ends of nearby streets. Work would be confined to local streets used primarily for access to abutting residences; improvements to major collectors or arterials is not included in this alternative. Use of Housing and Community Development Act funds for these purposes is allowed under those provisions of the guidelines which include the construction and reconstruction of streets, street lights and pedestrian walkways among the eligible activities.
The beneficial impacts of the street improvement alternative embrace those positive impacts analyzed for the street improvement programs of the proposed plan, including the hydrology/water quality, energy, and traffic categories. From a planning viewpoint there is the additional benefit in that a street improvement alternative allows for coordinated efforts between neighborhood projects without treating each neighborhood's local traffic problems in isolation.
The adverse impacts of the street alternative encompass the negative impacts previously identified for the street improvement programs of the proposed plan. Negative impacts are not likely to accompany the bulk of the work performed under this alternative. Impacts are most significant when a new street is extended across undeveloped land; repairing and curbing will have only minor impacts.
This alternative, concentrating on physical improvements to local streets and sidewalks, is prevented, thereby, from fulfilling the more personal needs of residents in complete contrast to the social services alternative discussed below. While the street alternative has hardly any of the adverse impacts associated with the proposed plan, its singular objective may be viewed as not directly reaching many problems responsible for neighborhood blight.
